Raincloud plot

Source: R/geom_raincloud.R
geom_raincloud.Rd

Create a raincloud plot, which shows, for each group, the distribution of a numeric variable as a half violin (the cloud), the median with quantile intervals, and the raw observations as jittered points (the rain). The half violins and the intervals are drawn with geom_violinhalf(), so this function needs the ggdist package (version 3.3.3 or later). Each half violin extends to the right of its position (up, in a horizontal plot), and the points are jittered in a band on the other side, from 0.45 to 0.05 times the spacing of the categorical axis away from the position (or closer, for a narrow width). Optionally, the quantile intervals of each group can be shaded behind its points, for example as a background for estimated means and their confidence intervals. Dodged groups, as with fill mapped to a second variable, are not supported: the half violins are dodged, but the points and the shading of all groups at a position share one band, and the shading pools their values. The categorical axis must be discrete.

Usage

geom_raincloud(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  trim = TRUE,
  scale = c("area", "count", "width"),
  interval = TRUE,
  shade = NULL,
  seed = 1,
  ...,
  size_points = 1.5,
  alpha_points = 0.5,
  color_points = NULL,
  fill_shade = "grey50",
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping

Set of aesthetic mappings created by aes(). If specified and inherit.aes = TRUE (the default), it is combined with the default mapping at the top level of the plot. You must supply mapping if there is no plot mapping.

data

The data to be displayed in this layer. There are three options:

If NULL, the default, the data is inherited from the plot data as specified in the call to ggplot().

A data.frame, or other object, will override the plot data. All objects will be fortified to produce a data frame. See fortify() for which variables will be created.

A function will be called with a single argument, the plot data. The return value must be a data.frame, and will be used as the layer data. A function can be created from a formula (e.g. ~ head(.x, 10)).

trim

If TRUE (default), trim the tails of the half violins to the range of the data. If FALSE, extend the tails as ggplot2::geom_violin() does.

scale

If "area" (default), all half violins have the same area (before trimming the tails). If "count", areas are scaled proportionally to the number of observations. If "width", all half violins have the same maximum width.

interval

Logical. If TRUE (default), add the median and the 66% and 95% quantile intervals of each group at its position, as in geom_violinhalf().

shade

A numeric vector of coverages between 0 and 1, such as c(0.5, 0.8, 0.95). For each coverage, a rectangle behind the points of each group spans the central quantile interval of the group's values (stats::quantile(), type 7, without missing values), computed on the scale of the axis (after a transformation such as scale_y_log10()). Each rectangle has an alpha of 0.2, so the inner intervals, where the rectangles overlap, are shaded darker. If NULL (default), nothing is shaded.

seed

The random seed of the jitter of the points, a single whole number. The same seed gives the same jitter.

...

Other arguments passed to geom_violinhalf(), such as fill, alpha, bw, or .width. They do not reach the points or the shading, except for width, height, and na.rm. So position moves only the half violins and the intervals. A width (or height, in a horizontal plot) is the width of a whole violin, as in geom_violinhalf(), so each half violin and the band of the points take half of it. flip = TRUE is not supported, because the half violins would cover the points.

size_points, alpha_points, color_points

The size, transparency, and color of the points. If one of them is NULL, the points take the matching aesthetic (size, alpha, or colour) instead. By default, only color_points is NULL.

fill_shade

The fill color of the shaded intervals.

show.legend

Should the half violins be included in the legends? The points and the shading are never included.

inherit.aes

If FALSE, overrides the default aesthetics, rather than combining with them. This is most useful for helper functions that define both data and aesthetics and shouldn't inherit behaviour from the default plot specification, e.g. annotation_borders().

Value

A list of ggplot2 layers.

Examples

library(ggplot2)
library(see)

ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_raincloud() +
  theme_modern()


# A horizontal raincloud plot
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Species, fill = Species)) +
  geom_raincloud() +
  theme_modern()


# Shade the 50%, 80%, and 95% quantile intervals behind the points
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Length, colour = Species)) +
  geom_raincloud(shade = c(0.5, 0.8, 0.95)) +
  theme_modern()
